CANONICAL_NAME.value: MD5 (RFC 1321 reference implementation) -- a hash function whose collision resistance was broken

VERSION.value: RFC 1321 text including the reference implementation (appendix)

value.lineage: MD5 (Rivest, 1992, RFC 1321) was the default cryptographic hash for a decade: 128-bit digest, Merkle-Damgard over a 512-bit block compression function. Wang et al. published practical collisions in 2004-2005, and RFC 6151 records that MD5 is no longer acceptable where collision resistance is required. The fossil is the RFC's own reference C code -- the standard and its implementation in one artifact.

value.built_to: produce a short fixed-length fingerprint of a message that is infeasible to forge or collide
value.pressure: fingerprints had to be cheap enough to hash whole files while resisting an adversary searching for two messages with one digest
value.success_means: matching the RFC's published digests, and no feasible way to find two messages sharing one

value.pressure: an adversary free to choose both messages (collision), with growing compute and improving differential cryptanalysis
value.failure_condition: collision resistance fell -- Wang et al. produced colliding pairs; MD5 is now unsuitable for signatures or certificates while remaining a correct checksum

ANCESTRY.value: MD5 (Rivest, 1992, RFC 1321) was the default cryptographic hash for a decade: 128-bit digest, Merkle-Damgard over a 512-bit block compression function. Wang et al. published practical collisions in 2004-2005, and RFC 6151 records that MD5 is no longer acceptable where collision resistance is required. The fossil is the RFC's own reference C code -- the standard and its implementation in one artifact.

evidence.ref: RFC 6151 (2011), Updated Security Considerations for MD5 and HMAC-MD5
evidence.says: MD5 is no longer acceptable where collision resistance is required, and new protocol designs should not use it.

evidence.ref: Wang & Yu, How to Break MD5 and Other Hash Functions, EUROCRYPT 2005
evidence.says: Practical collisions for MD5 can be constructed, breaking its collision resistance.

inspected_files: rfc1321.txt section 3 (lines 119-295) in full; appendix code skimmed
cut.note: a Merkle-Damgard construction with a four-round compression function; the organs are the padding rule, the chaining, the nonlinear round functions, the message-word schedule with rotation constants, and the sine-derived additive constants

provenance.grade_basis: Techne FOSSIL_PACKET.json PROVENANCE_GRADE where issued, else the record's handoff string mapped (populated per R34; Harmonia may re-grade)

organs.mechanism: append a single 1 bit, then 0 bits until the length is 448 mod 512, then the 64-bit original length (low word first); padding is applied even when the length is already 448 mod 512, so every message has a distinct padded form
assumptions: the length suffix is what prevents trivial extension of the padded message into another valid padded message (but not the length-extension attack on the digest itself)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: unambiguous parsing of the last block
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the Merkle-Damgard length-extension property: knowing H(m) and |m| one can compute H(m || pad || m') without m

organs.human_name: Steps 3-5: the (A,B,C,D) buffer, the per-block save/add-back, the output
organs.mechanism: four 32-bit registers start at fixed constants; for each block the registers are saved, 64 operations mix the block in, then the saved values are ADDED back (feed-forward) so the compression function is not invertible from its output; the final registers are the digest
assumptions: collision resistance of the whole follows from that of the compression function (Merkle 1989, Damgard 1989) -- the assumption that failed in practice
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: streaming: a message of any length is hashed with 128 bits of state
organs.failure_landscape: the record's own: differential collisions in the compression function (Wang & Yu 2004) break the construction; the feed-forward does not help
organs.human_prior: Merkle-Damgard; the four-register width chosen for 32-bit machines of 1991

organs.human_name: Step 4: F, G, H, I; [abcd k s i] = a = b + ((a + f(b,c,d) + X[k] + T[i]) <<< s)
organs.mechanism: each of 64 operations updates one register from the other three: add a bitwise selector/majority/parity/xor-or function of (b,c,d), a message word X[k], and a table constant T[i]; rotate left by s; add b; the registers rotate roles (ABCD, DABC, CDAB, BCDA); rounds use F (if-then-else), G (a different selector), H (parity), I (y xor (x or not z))
organs.input: the block X[0..15], the four registers
assumptions: the text's own claim: if the inputs' bits are independent and unbiased, each function's output bits are too
the mix of boolean functions, modular addition and rotation is 'ARX plus boolean' -- fast on 32-bit hardware
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: speed on 1991 hardware with 'strong' mixing by the standards of the time
organs.failure_landscape: the differential path that breaks MD5 goes through these round functions' weak diffusion in rounds 1-2
organs.human_prior: Rivest's design; the round functions are chosen for bitwise-parallel nonlinearity
organs.source_boundary: the four function definitions and the 64 operations

organs.human_name: the k and s columns of the 64 operations (rounds: k = i, 5i+1, 3i+5, 7i mod 16; s = 7/12/17/22, 5/9/14/20, 4/11/16/23, 6/10/15/21)
organs.mechanism: each round visits all 16 message words once in a fixed permutation (identity, then strides 5, 3, 7 with offsets) and uses four rotation amounts cycling per operation; the schedule is a constant table, not derived from the message
assumptions: the four strides are coprime to 16 so every word is used exactly once per round
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: every message bit influences every round
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: a fixed schedule lets an attacker choose message differences that cancel across rounds

organs.mechanism: T[i] = floor(2^32 x |sin(i)|), i in radians, i = 1..64; the constants are published as derived from a transcendental function so that no hidden structure can be suspected in their choice
assumptions: a publicly derivable constant is trusted more than an arbitrary one (a social mechanism encoded in arithmetic)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: trust in the design; breaks the symmetry between operations

rejected_cuts.evidence: skimmed only; the appendix code implements the five steps above and is the natural Stage C body (it compiles anywhere with a C compiler -- not on M3)
rejected_cuts.note: not rejected on the merits; unread this pass

rejected_cuts.evidence: padding, chaining, rounds, schedule and constants are separately replaceable; SHA-1 keeps the first two and changes the rest

pressures.condition: the organism maps any input to n bits; an adversary who knows the map fully tries to produce two inputs with the same output (collision) or an input for a given output (preimage); the organism's cost per input bit is bounded
pressures.resource_or_constraint: n bits of state; a few operations per input word; the design is public
pressures.failure_condition: a collision found in far fewer than 2^(n/2) trials
pressures.world_punishes: linear diffusion, weak nonlinearity, message-independent schedules
pressures.observable_consequence: trials to first collision under a differential search vs the birthday bound; MD5's own history (2^64 -> 2^24) is the measured failure
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: a world where the adversary cannot read the design
pressures.cheat_control: an organism that is a random oracle (a world-supplied lookup) must show the birthday bound; MD5 must show the known 2^24 differential shortcut: if the world cannot distinguish them, it is not exerting the adversarial pressure
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: cryptographic message digest (Rivest 1992; broken Wang & Yu 2004)
